This mechanism produces magnon currents even without conventional driving forces such as temperature gradients or chemical potential differences. We then introduce motion-induced parametric instabilities. When the emergent scale becomes sufficiently large to resonantly create magnon pairs, the perturbative description breaks down, and the magnonic vacuum becomes unstable. This instability occurs above a critical velocity threshold and leads to spontaneous magnon-pair creation. Connections to related phenomena, including quantum friction, Cherenkov emission, and Zel'dovich superradiance, are also highlighted. The concept of an emergent energy scale provides a unifying framework for understanding transport phenomena and instabilities in quantum systems with relative motion.

items.title: Topological zero-reflection points in multi-terminal quantum wire junctions
authors: Abhiram Soori, Udit Khanna, Diptiman Sen
items.summary: We study scattering in noninteracting multi-terminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for $N \ge 4$ terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the $(E,t')$ parameter space, where $E$ is the incident particle energy and $t'$ is the junction hopping amplitude. These points exhibit an even-odd dependence on $N$ and converge asymptotically to a common limiting value in the large-$N$ limit. We show that the reflectionless points are characterized by an integer winding number associated with the phase of the reflection amplitude, providing a topological description for their stability against weak on-site disorder. We also consider junctions with broken time-reversal symmetry and find that a magnetic flux can induce additional reflectionless points, including for the $N = 3$ case. For a four-terminal junction threaded by a $\pi$-flux, we identify a unique parameter regime in which the reflection amplitude vanishes over the entire energy band. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures through the behavior of Friedel oscillations and examine the stability of these reflectionless points in the presence of weak interactions.

items.title: Magnetic Field Control of the N\'eel Vector and Magnon Visibility in Altermagnetic MnTe
authors: Tobias Weber, Niclas Heinsdorf, Shane Smolenski, Sawyer Beltz, Alexandre Ivanov, Andrea Piovano, Victor Mecoli, Sean Knapp, Ruiqi Tang, Amir Henderson, A. K. M. Ashiquzzaman Shawon, Taylor Pierce-James, Na Hyun Jo, Denis Karaiskaj
items.summary: Altermagnetic order gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting of electronic and magnonic excitations even in the absence of a net magnetization. Here, we investigate the magnetic field dependence of the spin-wave spectrum of altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe using inelastic neutron scattering and linear spin-wave theory. An in-plane magnetic field continuously reorients the N\'eel vector by overcoming the weak crystalline anisotropy, while remaining small compared with the dominant exchange scale. We find that this reorientation leaves the magnon energies and line widths essentially unchanged, but strongly modifies the measured spectral intensity through the transverse-momentum projection. Our results demonstrate a clear separation between the soft orientational degree of freedom of the antiferromagnetic order and the robust exchange-dominated chiral magnon spectrum. This combination establishes $\alpha$-MnTe as a platform for reconfigurable magnon coupling, in which external fields tune how excitations interact with polarized probes without substantially altering their frequency or coherence.

items.title: Quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4
authors: Mika Tanabe, Momoko Tsujimoto, Kenichi Kinugawa
items.summary: We show the emergence of a quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4 obeying Boltzmann statistics, in the absence of atomic exchange. Using path integral centroid molecular dynamics simulations over 0.1-3.3 K and 1-60 bar, we investigate the transport properties of two distinct liquid states: the low quantum dispersion liquid (LQDL) and the high quantum dispersion liquid (HQDL). While LQDL exhibits conventional liquid behavior consistent with the Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, HQDL emerges at lower temperatures and displays anomalous gas-like transport characterized by superdiffusion and ultralow viscosity, accompanied by a breakdown of the SE relation. This counterintuitive emergence of gas-like dynamics upon cooling reflects the dominant role of nuclear quantum fluctuations, in contrast to thermal fluctuations at higher temperatures. Across the LQDL-HQDL boundary, we identify a transport crossover marked by a qualitative change in the velocity autocorrelation function (VAF), a transition in the Prandtl number, and the emergence of transport minima in shear and kinematic viscosities, thermal conductivity, and thermal diffusivity. These minima reflect a crossover from liquid-like to gas-like transport upon cooling in the low-temperature subcritical region, in addition to the universal transport minima observed in the supercritical regime. The transition from oscillatory to monotonic VAF defines a second Frenkel line, distinct from the conventional Frenkel line observed in the supercritical region. LQDL is a heat-transport-dominated dissipative fluid, whereas HQDL is a momentum-dominated inertial fluid. These results demonstrate that nuclear quantum fluctuations alone induce gas-like liquid behavior and provide a unified picture of transport phenomena in distinguishable helium-4 without superfluidity.

items.title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
authors: Prashant Dwivedi, Alberto Fraile, Tomas Polcar
items.summary: Amorphous refractory metal coatings combine high hardness with chemical inertness, yet their metastability makes them prone to mechanically induced crystallisation (devitrification) under contact loading, and how readily such a glass re-orders to its parent body centred cubic (bcc) crystal is unknown across the refractory series. We prepared amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta and W by melt quenching to 300 K, benchmarked each interatomic potential against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions and self-diffusion coefficients, and probed them by large scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation. Indentation drives a localised amorphous to bcc transformation by bulk nucleation, growth and coalescence. A crystal forming ability (CFA), the maximum slope of the sigmoidal bcc fraction versus depth curve, spans about a factor of four and decreases as V > Mo > Nb > Ta > W; it falls with indenter velocity as CFA scales as v^(-m), with a mean exponent of 1.08, so CFA.v is nearly constant and the transformation rate is almost velocity independent. Transforming atoms carry excess non affine displacement and local shear strain, not hydrostatic pressure, marking a shear associated displacive pathway; the bulk driving force is largest for the most resistant element, W, so resistance tracks cohesive bond strength rather than the thermodynamic driving force. Early bcc like order correlates with the sharpness and depth of the transition, whereas the mechanical work to half transformation correlates with the peak density of persistent bcc clusters. A cluster population balance links nucleation, growth and coalescence to a terminal microstructure whose completeness does not follow the CFA order.

items.title: EBSD and Subtle Crystallographic Differences - A Study of Resolving Interlayer Spacings in Nb-Ni and Nb-Co mu-phases
authors: Lukas Berners, Nisa Ulumuddin, Annika Baum, Silvia Richter, Khalil Rejiba, Joshua Spille, Siyuan Zhang, Christina Scheu, Joachim Mayer, Benjamin Berkels, T. Ben Britton, Sandra Korte-Kerzel
items.summary: In ordered intermetallics, slight variations in lattice site occupancy and specific interlayer spacings have been identified as the sources of significant changes in critical resolved shear stress and therefore how a given phase may affect alloy properties. So far, atom positions and lattice site occupancies have traditionally been characterised by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), which are methods that offer either local detail or high statistical significance but not both. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), by contrast, provides high spatial resolution across large sample areas and therefore, has the potential to enable the local investigation of interlayer spacing and site lattice occupancy with improved statistical reliability. The objectives of the study are to benchmark EBSDs capability for resolving these subtle features and to correlate them with compositional and mechanical properties. In this case study, we therefore show that EBSD can resolve key crystallographic features of mu-phase intermetallics, specifically interlayer spacings. We combine pattern matching with large-scale dynamical simulations of template libraries guided by XRD based information on lattice parameters. For this, we generate structures that vary in the spacing between triple-layer and Kagome layer and in the site lattice occupancy of the 3a site. This approach successfully predicts the change of interlayer spacing between Kagome and triple layers in Nb-Co and Nb-Ni mu-phases, in good agreement with XRD and HR-TEM.

items.title: Thermal Hall Signatures of Distinct Schwinger-Boson Flux Sectors on the Honeycomb Lattice
items.summary: Thermal transport offers a bulk probe of charge-neutral excitations in frustrated magnets. It remains challenging, however, to determine whether such transport can distinguish different parton mean-field structures of the same spin system. This question is particularly relevant on the honeycomb lattice, where distinct $0$-flux, $\pi$-flux, and chiral $\pi/2$-flux sectors have been proposed. In this paper, we compare self-consistent saddle-point solutions in these three sectors for a frustrated $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model with a next-nearest-neighbor Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and a perpendicular magnetic field. Using finite-temperature Schwinger-boson mean-field theory and the Kubo formula for bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems, we evaluate the intrinsic spinon thermal Hall conductivity. At a common parameter point where all three branches remain gapped, the $0$-flux response is positive and the $\pi$-flux response is negative for $D>0$ and $h>0$ under the sign conventions used in this paper, whereas the $\pi/2$-flux response changes sign with increasing temperature. We further show that a projective symmetry combining a sixfold rotation with time reversal forces the zero-field response of a fixed chiral $\pi/2$-flux domain to vanish. Within the mean-field regime examined in this paper, the sign and temperature dependence of $\kappa_{xy}/T$ therefore provide a flux-sensitive transport signature.

items.title: Decoding Oxygen K-edge Fingerprints of NCM-811 Degradation via Ab Initio Many-Body Theory and High-Throughput Screening of Crystal Proxies
authors: Daniel Duarte-Ruiz, Timo Reents, Elmar Kataev, Raul Garcia-Diez, Regan G. Wilks, Marcus Baer, Caterina Cocchi
items.summary: The degradation of LiNi$_{0.8}$Co$_{0.1}$Mn$_{0.1}$O$_2$ (NCM-811) in Li-ion batteries produces complex transition-metal oxides and binary phases that fundamentally limit cathode performance. While identifying these degradation products via X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is essential for mitigating electrochemical performance loss, interpretation remains challenging due to the structural complexity of real-world samples. In this work, we present an integrated theoretical-experimental framework combining high-resolution oxygen K-edge XAS with \textit{ab initio} simulations based on many-body perturbation theory and high-throughput screening from density functional theory. We first evaluate the spectroscopic fingerprints of eight layered, spinel, and nominal rock-salt reference oxides, identifying discrepancies between the idealized single-crystal bulk phase and experimental spectra. Using high-throughput screening to analyze the oxygen $p$-projected density of states of 38 distinct polymorphs of NiO, CoO, and MnO, we propose that the spectral differences can emerge, among other factors, from local structural variations represented here by simplified structural proxies. Our work establishes a viable and rigorous computational pathway to interpret the complex landscape of degraded battery materials.

items.title: Sequential Retrieval in Dense Associative Memory: Asymptotic Dynamics and Storage Capacity
authors: Mao Mishima, Ayaka Sakata, Kazushi Mimura
items.summary: We study the retrieval dynamics of an $n$-body asymmetric dense associative memory model, in which sequential retrieval is implemented by shifting one pattern index in the higher-order Hebbian interaction. The model exhibits sequential retrieval of the stored patterns, and the retrieval state corresponds to a stable limit-cycle attractor. The storage capacity is defined as the maximum loading rate for which this limit cycle remains stable. Using generating functional analysis, we derive the dynamical equations describing the sequential retrieval state. The generating functional analysis reveals that the retarded self-interaction term vanishes in the asymmetric model, and the resulting overlap dynamics is reproduced by an Amari-Maginu-type signal-to-noise analysis. Also, we find that for the interaction order $n\ge 3$, the normalized storage capacity decreases monotonically with increasing interaction order, in contrast to symmetric Modern Hopfield models.

items.title: Determining the j-Specific Unoccupied 5f Electronic Structure in Actinides
items.summary: An empirical comparison of high resolution M4,5 X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), based upon High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detection (HERFD), with Bremsstrahlung Isochromat Spectroscopy (BIS), the high energy variant of Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy (IPES), of various actinide materials is presented here. It will be shown that XAS-HERFD is essentially the j-specific version of BIS, providing a direct measure of the separate 5f5/2 and 5f7/2 Unoccupied Density of States (UDOS).

items.title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
items.summary: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. The total number of dipoles in the set of Fermi seas forming the two-dimensional ground state equals the number of electrons in the system and the density of states at the Fermi level is that of a two-dimensional Fermi gas. The model is obtained by generalizing, or rather adopting, the existing exact solution on a thin, but not too thin, torus to the two-dimensional bulk case.

items.title: A Hierarchy of Exact Lower Bounds on the Laughlin Spectral Gap
items.summary: We develop a bootstrap approach to deriving lower bounds on the spectral gap of the first Haldane pseudopotential Hamiltonian on the sphere with $N_\Phi$ flux quanta for arbitrary $N_\Phi$, including in the thermodynamic limit $N_\Phi \to \infty$. This method can in principle be generalized to pseudopotentials describing other model wavefunctions such as the Moore--Read state or Read--Rezayi sequence. Our approach is based on Knabe's observation that if $H$ is a Hamiltonian with ground state energy zero then the spectral gap is at least $\epsilon > 0$ if and only if $H^2 \succeq \epsilon H$. To show this inequality, we split $H^2$ into two parts, one that can be analytically bounded and another that can be bounded using a finite semidefinite program (SDP). Crucially, the size of this program is determined only by cutoff parameters, and the program depends on $N_\Phi$ only parametrically, allowing us to obtain numerically exact (up to solver precision) lower bounds on the gap. In order to turn these numerical bounds into mathematically rigorous results, we introduce an algorithm that can produce nearly-optimal exact interior feasible points for large rational SDPs even if the affine constraints are highly redundant and ill-conditioned. We additionally provide an algorithm that establishes the rank stability of the SDP in the $N_\Phi \to \infty$ limit, which is needed to certify the bound in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond establishing a Laughlin gap greater than $1/100$ in the thermodynamic limit and revealing a potential method for deriving spectral gap lower bounds for other pseudopotentials, our work provides a general method for turning numerical SDP bounds into rigorous mathematical proofs, which may have wide applicability. In particular, this work demonstrates that bootstrap methods can be used to rigorously resolve major open problems in quantum many-body physics.

items.title: Active tissue mechanics drives a diversity of collective flows in uniaxially compressed 3D spheroids
authors: Liyang Wang, Shabeeb Ameen, J. M. Schwarz, Tao Zhang
items.summary: Compression can enhance or suppress cell motion and induce coherent rotation in tissue spheroids, but the physical factors governing these responses remain unclear. Using a minimal three-dimensional active vertex model, we examine how tissue mechanics, active driving, and directional alignment shape the response to uniaxial compression. Without alignment, compression enhances transverse motion in solid-like spheroids throughout the tested activity range, whereas fluid-like spheroids switch from acceleration at low activity to slowing at high activity. Changes in contact persistence connect these responses to neighbor exchange. Passive five-cell calculations show that compression reshapes local rearrangement barriers depending on geometry and loading direction; a high-strain increase in the fluid-like mean coexists with many low-barrier paths. With strong alignment, compression induces coherent rotation in solid-like spheroids, while fluid-like spheroids show no comparable rotation. Rotating solids retain more persistent cell contacts than fluids and develop tangential organization of peripheral cells. Controlled perturbations reveal that compression softens a differential-twist mode and activity slows its relaxation. Together, these results link activity-dependent reversal of the speed response and compression-induced coherent rotation to contact dynamics, local rearrangement costs, and active driving. Our findings demonstrate that one minimal model, with parameters representing effective mechanical and active tissue properties, captures diverse collective responses to compression and provides a framework for predicting how different tissues respond to mechanical loading.

items.title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Rustam Arabov, Konstantin Sozykin, Alexander Shapeev, Nikita Rybin
items.summary: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

items.title: Two-stage Slowdown of Vacancy-mediated Diffusion in a Lattice Gas Model with Quenched Disorder and Spins
items.summary: We present a lattice gas model with random interactions quenched in space and spins quenched to the particles. The vacancy-mediated diffusion is studied in equilibrium. A two-stage slowdown is witnessed in both the mean squared displacement and the spatial overlaps. We demonstrate that the plateaus are due to anti-correlation at the corresponding length scale. The anti-correlation diminishes quickly with increasing lag time. A broad and yet finite distribution of the survival function of vacancies suggests their normal diffusion at large time limit. Our model can serve as a new playground for understanding hierarchical dynamics in glassy-like dynamical systems.

items.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
items.summary: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

items.title: Extremal and global-time statistics of sluggish random walks with stochastic resetting
items.summary: We study a sluggish random walk, whose diffusivity decreases as a power law with distance from the origin, under Poissonian resetting to the origin. Using a mapping to a signed Bessel process and renewal theory, we obtain exact results for the maximum trajectory value in a finite window, the time at which it occurs, and the time of the last visit to the origin. Resetting changes the growth of the typical maximum from a power law in time to a power of its logarithm. The centered maximum approaches a Gumbel law, whose width shrinks in physical space for any positive sluggishness exponent, unlike the Brownian case. In the Bessel coordinate, the probability that the maximum exceeds a value growing in proportion to the observation window length decays exponentially, with a rate that has a second-order dynamical transition and is independent of sluggishness. The time of the maximum is uniform in the bulk, with boundary layers that shift its mean above the midpoint logarithmically with window length. The time since the last visit to the origin follows a Gamma law with a sluggishness-dependent shape. Reflection symmetry makes the last-visit time uncorrelated with the occupation time of the positive half-line.

items.title: Many-Body Bound States in the Continuum
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Yuto Ashida, Masahito Ueda
items.summary: -cross Abstract: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a spatially localized energy eigenstate embedded in a continuous spectrum of extended eigenstates. While diverse types of single-particle BICs have been reported in the literature, understanding how such localization persists in interacting many-body systems remains a fundamental problem. Here, we present numerical evidence and a perturbative analysis supporting the existence of many-body BICs in a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard chain with an attractive impurity potential, a system previously known to host a BIC in the two-particle sector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Bethe-type construction of the known two-particle BIC breaks down already for three particles even for arbitrary finite superpositions of Bethe waves. The resulting BICs violate the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis for several local one- and two-body observables, leading to nonthermal dynamics from experimentally accessible initial states.

items.title: Detailed balance in large language model-driven agents
authors: Zhuo-Yang Song, Qing-Hong Cao, Ming-xing Luo, Hua Xing Zhu
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven agents are emerging as a powerful new paradigm for solving complex problems. Despite the empirical success of these practices, a theoretical framework to understand and unify their macroscopic dynamics remains lacking. This paper proposes a method based on the least action principle to estimate the underlying generative directionality of LLMs embedded within agents. By experimentally measuring the transition probabilities between LLM-generated states, we report evidence consistent with a tendency toward detailed balance in LLM-generated transitions, indicating that LLM generation may not be achieved by generally learning rule sets and strategies, but rather by implicitly learning a class of underlying potential functions that may transcend different LLM architectures and prompt templates. To our knowledge, this provides an effective macroscopic description of LLM generative dynamics that does not depend on specific model details. This work is an attempt to establish a macroscopic dynamics theory of complex AI systems, aiming to elevate the study of AI agents from a collection of engineering practices to a science built on effective measurements that are predictable and quantifiable.

items.title: Protonic thermoelectric effect of Superionic H$_2$O and magnetic field generation in Uranus and Neptune
authors: Daohong Liu, Wei Zhang, Yu He, Xinzhuan Guo, Chuanyu Zhang, Yang Sun
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The origin of the anomalous magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune, with significant tilts and multi-dipole configurations, is central to understanding the internal structure and evolution of the ice giants. Recent investigations confirmed that superionic H$_2$O ice is thermodynamically stable and constitutes the dominant H$_2$O phase within their icy mantles. Here, we use deep learning and ab initio molecular dynamics to investigate the thermal and protonic transport properties of superionic H$_2$O ice. We demonstrate that superionic H$_2$O ice exhibits a pronounced protonic thermoelectric effect, with a maximum Seebeck coefficient that can reach $\sim 620$ $\mu$V K$^{-1}$ within the interior of Uranus, whereas Neptune's is lower, within the range of 570-585 $\mu$V K$^{-1}$. Consequently, the temperature gradients in the icy mantles can induce proton migration, thereby driving magnetic field generation. Based on this mechanism, and within a dipolar approximation that captures the mean field, the disparities in mean dipolar magnetic field strength between Uranus and Neptune can be explained exclusively by their differing internal temperature gradients, and the predicted mean field strengths are comparable to those observed by Voyager 2.

items.title: Shortcuts to Adiabaticity via Adaptive Quantum Zeno Measurements
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Stroboscopic measurements of a time-dependent projector generate a quantum Zeno dynamics whose effective Hamiltonian is the Kato-Avron Hamiltonian for parallel transport, which reduces to counterdiabatic driving in the case of a nonselective measurement of the instantaneous eigenprojectors of the system. The same generator arises under continuous monitoring of a time-dependent observable and under a time-varying complex absorbing potential. Departures from the ideal Zeno limit are governed, in all three settings, by a single positive leakage operator with a dynamical and a purely geometric contribution. Matching the corresponding generators yields a model-independent generalized Schulman relation for the quantum Zeno dynamics in the three scenarios, and a purely geometric bound on the measurement resources needed to steer a subspace along a prescribed path.

items.title: Urban scaling and the dynamics of individual cities
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Cities are often compared through scaling laws, usually expressed as power-law relations between population size and aggregate urban quantities related to infrastructure, socioeconomic activity, or environmental impacts. These laws are influential because their exponent is often interpreted as describing what happens when a city grows, with implications for urban theory, planning, and policy. Here, we show that this interpretation is generally misleading. An exponent measured by comparing many cities at one date does not, in general, describe the trajectory of any individual city. Instead, it reflects a statistical pattern produced by cities with different histories, constraints, institutions, and growth paths. Apparent sublinear or superlinear scaling can therefore arise even when individual cities follow simpler dynamics, as we show for the area--population relation. Cross-sectional scaling laws can reveal system-level regularities, but should not be used alone to infer growth mechanisms or guide policy for a given city.

items.title: Simple slow operators and quantum thermalization
authors: Tian-Hua Yang, Ethan Jeon, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Dmitry A. Abanin
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We establish a rigorous operator-space condition for the thermalization of typical initial states. We introduce a concept of simple slow operators (SSOs), defined as operators that evolve slowly under Heisenberg-picture dynamics and have significant small-sized components. We show that the non-thermalization of typical initial states drawn from a weakly entangled state ensemble implies the existence of SSOs; equivalently, the absence of SSOs implies that typical initial states thermalize. We establish these results by introducing the concept of an ensemble variance norm of an operator, defined as the typical magnitude of the expectation value of that operator with respect to states in the ensemble. For low-entanglement ensembles, the norm is related to operator sizes, allowing us to establish a direct link between operator dynamics and thermalization.

items.title: Operator space transport in collective spin Lindbladians
authors: Dominik Nemeth, Ahsan Nazir, Robert-Jan Slager, Alessandro Principi
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Boundary time crystals (BTCs) are paradigmatic examples of continuous time crystals that emerge in collective, dissipative quantum systems. Their microscopic origin, however, remains obscured by the complexity of Lindbladian many-body dynamics and has largely been investigated through semiclassical and numerical approaches. Here, we develop an exact operator space framework for collective spin Lindbladians based on irreducible tensor representations. We map the Lindbladian dynamics onto a local non-Hermitian hopping problem, where weak symmetries impose selection rules on operator transport, while the hopping amplitudes and their relative strengths determine the resulting dynamical regimes. We identify the microscopic ingredients that distinguish models supporting conventional collective precession from those supporting BTC dynamics. Our approach further reveals how non-unital dissipation can provide a source for the traceless operator subspace, providing a microscopic mechanism for the reduced sensitivity of BTC dynamics to initial conditions beyond mean-field descriptions. More broadly, our results establish operator space transport as a general perspective for understanding dissipative many-body dynamics and its connections to non-Hermitian phenomena.

items.title: Discovering quantum phenomena with Interpretable Machine Learning
authors: Paulin de Schoulepnikoff, Hendrik Poulsen Nautrup, Hans J. Briegel, Gorka Mu\~noz-Gil
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Interpretable machine learning techniques are becoming essential tools for extracting physical insights from complex quantum data. We build on recent advances in variational autoencoders to demonstrate that such models can learn physically meaningful and interpretable representations from a broad class of unlabeled quantum datasets. From raw measurement data alone, the learned representation reveals rich information about the underlying structure of quantum phase diagrams. We further augment the learning pipeline with symbolic methods, enabling the discovery of compact analytical descriptors that serve as order parameters for the distinct regimes emerging in the learned representations. We demonstrate the framework on experimental Rydberg-atom snapshots, classical shadows of the cluster Ising model, and hybrid discrete-continuous fermionic data, revealing previously unreported phenomena such as a corner-ordering pattern in the Rydberg arrays. These results establish a general framework, which constitutes an important step toward the autonomous discovery of physical descriptors from diverse quantum datasets. All methods are available through qdisc, an open-source Python library designed to make these tools accessible to the broader community.

items.title: Where solitons are in a KdV soliton gas
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) equation is a paradigmatic model of integrable classical fields, with solitonic solutions where localised profiles interact by elastic, factorised scattering. When solitons interact, their shapes are modified, and individual solitons cannot be identified. This is a key problem in soliton gas where one needs a density of solitons per unit distance: can we locate asymptotic objects, quasiparticles, even at finite times in the macroscopic limit? Quasiparticles' positions should satisfy locality properties, the field in mesoscopic regions being determined by quasiparticles lying there. We solve this problem for the KdV equation. We define solitons' positions as functions of spectral and impact parameters via an expansion bijection generalising that of hard rods. These ``KdV rods'' solve the semiclassical Bethe equations, implementing the collision rate ansatz, and satisfy a repulsion condition generalising the rods' lengths to the KdV scattering shifts and related to the condensate condition. This gives an explicit characterisation of multi-soliton fields in terms of solitons' positions instead of impact parameters. We construct fluid-cell projections, that project out solitons lying outside mesoscopic regions: the resulting field is unchanged in this region and supported there up to small corrections. We show that in the weak limit, conserved densities are given by the empirical density for these solitons' positions. Thus we have associated a kinetic theory of quasiparticles to the KdV equation. The results hold under natural assumptions on spectral and impact parameters, and no randomness is required. Our proof is based on novel solitonic tau functions. This is a crucial step towards rigorously deriving the kinetic equation of the KdV soliton gas, first proposed by Gennady El in 2003. We believe the methods are generalisable to other solitonic models.

items.title: An Asymptotic Theory of Chain-of-Thought in In-Context Learning
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has become a widely used mechanism for eliciting multi-step reasoning in large language models by generating intermediate reasoning steps at inference time. Yet the scaling behavior of generalization with CoT depth remains poorly understood. To address this question, we study a theoretically solvable model of CoT for in-context weight prediction in linear regression, where test-time reasoning is represented as an iterative refinement of the weight-parameter estimate. Using tools from random matrix theory under high-dimensional asymptotics, we derive an exact formula for the generalization error as a function of reasoning depth, pretraining data amount, and context length. Our analysis reveals a sharp phase transition separating exponential and polynomial improvement, saturation, and overthinking, and characterizes how the optimal reasoning depth scales. We further show that deeper reasoning is most effective with sufficiently rich pretraining and in-context information, whereas limited pretraining or context makes longer reasoning prone to error amplification or saturation. We also validate these predictions through experiments on fully learned linear attention and softmax attention models. Our results provide a unified theoretical account of how test-time CoT depth affects generalization.

items.title: sft-wick: A formalism and package for Feynman-diagram expansion and evaluation in stochastic field theories
items.summary: -cross Abstract: When stochastic field dynamics are cast into a path-integral formulation, perturbation theory becomes systematic but the resulting expansion quickly grows combinatorially large. The setting targeted here includes fields with several components and several dimensions, matrix propagators, tensor-valued couplings, and non-Gaussian driving noise specified by arbitrary n-point cumulants. Wick pairings grow factorially, and component indices must be routed through the tensor-valued vertices. The useful output is not a raw contraction list, but a diagram table: one entry per topology, with multiplicities, coupling sums, signs, and causal constraints resolved. We present sft-wick, an open-source Python package that constructs these diagram tables and computes their integrals numerically. Given an action and an observable, it enumerates topologically distinct Feynman diagrams, derives their algebraic coefficients, and evaluates the resulting diagram integrals from user-supplied response and cumulant functions. The core algorithm enumerates spatial topologies before routing component indices, avoiding contraction-by-contraction Wick expansion. Response-field constraints, including vanishing response-response contractions, the Ito prescription, and the absence of causal response loops, are enforced during enumeration. Predictions are validated against direct Langevin simulations in two worked examples, with Gaussian and with non-Gaussian driving noise, and agree with the simulations within stated error budgets.

items.title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
authors: Zhenbang Gu, Ran Luo, Yi-Nan Wang, Yi Zhang
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $\Omega_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetilde{\Omega}_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such a non-split finite 2-group.

items.title: Entropy and Frenesy: the arrow and the bustle of time
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Nonequilibrium statistical mechanics is the science of time as it manifests itself in the transient or steady entropy producing dynamical condition of many-body systems. Beyond the vivid multiformity of the phenomena themselves, three foundational issues lie at its heart. The first question concerns the very origin of entropy production, which gives macroscopic processes their direction and thereby defines the arrow of time: how does an atomistic mechanical world give rise to dissipated heat, thermalization, and time-reversal symmetry breaking? The second asks why, far beyond the familiar behavior of equilibrium systems, driving or agitation may produce and select stable and functionally rich structures: what is it about far-from-equilibrium, low-entropy driving that unleashes the wealth and intricacy of the natural world? The third issue is partly methodological: to determine how, and for which subclass of such wildly diverse nonequilibrium systems, a systematic, unified description and modeling from first principles remains possible. This essay addresses these issues in an informal, semi-popular-science style, offering a personally engaging yet wide-ranging introduction to the complementary roles of entropy production and the less familiar, more recently coined notion of frenesy in the dynamical fluctuations of steadily driven systems. Together, we argue, they provide a more complete starting point for understanding physical time on mesoscopic to macroscopic scales.

items.title: Boundary-Canceled Score-Hamiltonian Sampling
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Diffusion sampling is related to imaginary-time quantum annealing through a forward/backward Schr\"odinger equation pair and its one-sided counterdiabatic connection. For a smooth, gapped Score-Hamiltonian path, the exact connection transports the target density at any evolution time. We apply quantum-annealing performance analysis to residuals from approximating this connection with a trained score. If the first $r$ terminal schedule derivatives vanish, the squared Hellinger error scales as $T^{-2r-2}$, with a prefactor determined by the terminal learning residual and inverse gaps. Direct two-dimensional imaginary-time evolution with one fixed neural score reproduces these powers and prefactors. Terminal schedule design thus suppresses the distributional effect of imperfect score learning without retraining the network.

items.title: Walshness: an intrinsic neural-network representability metric for quantum states
authors: Nisarga Paul, Kehuang Chen, Jessica K. Jiang, Haimeng Zhao, Di Luo
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Neural quantum states (NQS) have emerged as powerful representations of quantum states with rapidly expanding applications across quantum many-body physics. Yet our understanding of when neural networks can efficiently represent physical quantum states remains limited, in part due to the nonlinear parameterization of NQS, the intricate sign structure of quantum states, and the sensitive dependence on basis choice. We introduce Walshness, a complexity metric of a quantum state which quantifies whether it admits a compact neural-network representation. We rigorously prove that a general quantum many-body state admits an efficient NQS representation if it has bounded Walshness, and vice versa, for various NQS architectures. We provide an algorithm for finding the optimal basis by minimizing the energy of a corresponding classical spin model. This allows us to empirically improve the learnability of various physical quantum states, including ground states of the transverse-field Ising model and mixed-field toric code, often reducing infidelity by orders of magnitude, and generalizes the basis choice given by the well-known Marshall sign rule in frustrated antiferromagnets. Our results provide an intrinsic complexity metric for quantum states with provable connections to their neural-network representability.

items.title: Topological Superradiant Universality Classes in Cavity-Mediated Spin Chains
authors: Yunhao Liu, Sheng Yang, Mingyuan Chen, Xue-Jia Yu
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Superradiant phase transitions are fundamental phenomena in light-matter coupled systems. Here, we uncover a novel class of superradiant criticality that is topologically distinct from previously known superradiant transitions. Using cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains as an illustrative example, we numerically demonstrate that the critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase hosts robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, a feature absent in conventional superradiant transitions. Remarkably, although its local bulk critical properties are indistinguishable from those of the previously identified topologically trivial superradiant transition, the two criticalities cannot be smoothly connected without breaking the protecting symmetries or passing through a multicritical point. We further show that such topological superradiant criticality is generic, also occurring in cavity-mediated $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{}$ cluster-qudit chains, as supported by complementary lattice simulations.

items.title: A neural accelerated roughness-resolved Discrete Element Method (Rough-DEM) for modeling granular systems
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed roughness-resolved DEM (Rough-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE$^2$-like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a \textit{simple} representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that \textit{cannot always} be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for Rough-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.

items.title: On the uniqueness of translation-invariant ground states of the $S=1$ Heisenberg and $J$--$D$ antiferromagnetic chains
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Using the analytic machinery and numerical inputs of OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we prove uniqueness of the translation-invariant ground state of the infinite $S=1$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain and of the $J$-$D$ model for sufficiently small $|D|$. Uniqueness is among all translation-invariant ground states in the operator-algebraic sense, without assuming a gap or spin-rotation symmetry for a competing state. The proof combines concentration of the spatial transfer spectrum, an exponentially small low-temperature free-energy correction, and a Golden--Thompson comparison for separated local observables. The unique translation-invariant state is pure, locally unique and gapped, and continuous in $D$. The ground states of even periodic chains and odd open chains with equal positive endpoint fields converge to this state along their full sequences, uniformly in $D$, with a stretched-exponential local rate. Every choice of ground states of open chains without endpoint magnetic fields has the same local limit. These conclusions do not establish uniqueness among arbitrary nontranslation-invariant ground states of the infinite chain. The author formulated the problems and proposed the core strategies. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to developing the proofs and preparing the manuscript.

The Roaming Bethe Roots: An Effective Bethe Ansatz Beyond Integrability
authors: Wenlong Zhao, 文龙 赵, Yunfeng Jiang, 云峰 江, Rui-Dong Zhu and 睿东 朱
items.summary: We propose an effective Bethe ansatz (EBA) for solving quantum many-body systems near an integrable point. Our approach retains the functional form of the Bethe wave function while renormalizing the Bethe roots to account for integrability-breaking interactions. These effective roots are determined by minimizing physically motivated cost functions. The resulting off-shell Bethe states serve as approximate eigenstates of the non-integrable models. We assess the quality of the approximation using various physical observables, including the energy eigenvalue, state fidelity, and bipartite entanglement entropy. Our tests show that for models with weak integrability-breaking, the EBA provides a high-quality approximation to the exact eigenstates over a wide range of deformation parameters. In contrast, for models with strong integrability-breaking interactions, the efficacy of EBA degrades relatively quickly as the deformation parameter increases. The efficacy of the method thus offers a useful probe for characterizing the strength of integrability breaking. Within its regime of accuracy, it also provides a new representation of the eigenstates of nearly integrable models, enabling one to exploit the algebraic structure inherited from integrability.

items.title: Unveiling the Elusive Σ(1380) Resonance through Coupled-Channel Dynamics in Λ c + ηπ + Λ Reaction
authors: Wen-Tao Lyu, 文韬 吕, Si-Wei Liu, 思威 刘, Jia-Jun Wu, 佳俊 吴, De-Min Li, 德民 李, En Wang and 恩 王
items.summary: We investigate the Λc+ ηπ +Λ decay measured by the Belle and BESIII Collaborations, focusing on the possible role of the Σ(1380) state with spin-parity J P=1/2−. In our theoretical framework, the Λ(1670) and a0(980) are dynamically generated from meson–baryon and meson–meson final-state interactions, respectively, and the corresponding line shapes of these two states used here are applicable to all relevant hadronic reactions. Furthermore, the contributions from the intermediate Σ(1385) resonance and the possible Σ(1380) state are included explicitly. By comparing the invariant mass and angular distributions obtained with and without the Σ(1380) state, we demonstrate that this state plays an important role in improving the description of the experimental data. We also identify the kinematic regions most sensitive to the possible Σ(1380) contribution. Future high-precision measurements of this process will be instrumental for testing the existence of the Σ state with J P=1/2−.

items.title: Anomalous Local Enhancement of Thermal Conductivity under Nanoscale Hotspot: Spatial Inhomogeneity and Phonon Nonequilibrium in Silicon
authors: Yuxin Luo, 雨欣 罗, Shuai Wu, 帅 吴, Dongdong Kang, 冬冬 康, Xiaoxiang Yu, 晓翔 余, Jiayu Dai and 佳钰 戴
items.summary: The miniaturization of electronic devices gives rise to localized heat accumulation and thus nanoscale hotspots, triggering degenerated heat dissipation. However, the phonon transport mechanism and quantification of inhomogeneous nonequilibrium thermal conductivity remain elusive. Here, through molecular dynamics simulations of silicon thin film under nanoscale hotspot, we reveal a dramatic spatial inhomogeneity of cross-plane thermal conductivity κz under nanoscale hotspot excitation. Contrary to the conventional picture of phonon nonequilibrium simply suppressing heat transport, we find a non-monotonic spatial evolution: κz drops by up to 68% immediately beneath the hotspot (Lhot=10.9 nm), but subsequently recovers to exceed the uniform-heating baseline by 12% at a distance of ~40 nm, producing a maximum κz gradient of 3.2 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1—2.3 times that of uniform heating. Spectral decomposition indicates that longitudinal acoustic (LA) phonons dominate the anomalous local thermal conductivity enhancement. Modal temperature calculations reveal that the spatial relaxation of hotspot-induced LA phonon nonequilibrium matches well with the transition of thermal conductivity from suppression to anomalous enhancement. The magnitude of the spatial inhomogeneity diminishes with rising temperature (from 3.05 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1 at 300 K to 1.25 W·m−1·K−1·nm−1 at 600 K) due to increased anharmonic scattering. These findings challenge the common assumption of spatially uniform thermal conductivity in hotspot systems and provide a quantitative, spectrally resolved benchmark for thermal management of nanoscale devices.

items.title: Tunable Insulator–Metal Transitions and Flat Bands in Domain-Wall-Engineered Monolayer In2Se3
authors: Laiyuan Su, 来源 苏, Zhigang Gui, 志刚 桂, Li Huang and 丽 黄
items.summary: Ferroelectric domain walls (DWs) provide a promising platform for dynamically tuning electronic properties at the nanoscale. Using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that charged DWs in monolayer α-In2Se3 enable versatile band engineering across one and two dimensions. In one-dimensional DW arrays, the separation between tail-to-tail and head-to-head DWs controls the band gap: with increasing inter-wall distance, the valence and conduction bands, dominated respectively by the oppositely charged DWs, shift in opposite directions under contrasting local electrostatic potentials, leading to continuous gap reduction and ultimately an insulator-to-metal transition. Extending to two dimensions, periodic DW networks form a breathing kagome lattice, wherein each DW segment acts as a “super-atom”, yielding nearly dispersionless flat bands near the Fermi level. In addition, an isolated conduction band originating from the P↓ domains emerges near the Fermi level, with decreasing bandwidth as the superlattice size increases, giving rise to an effective triangular lattice. Our findings establish DW-engineered In2Se3 as a reconfigurable platform that bridges ferroelectric switching with quantum materials design, offering a promising route toward a possible platform for exploring emergent quantum phenomena in artificially engineered lattices.

items.title: A polymer-embedded molecular fuse for safer high-nickel lithium batteries
items.summary: Abstract Thermal runaway in high-energy lithium batteries is driven by autocatalytic radical reactions and flammable gas accumulation, posing a critical safety bottleneck for next-generation energy storage. Here we report a cathode-integrated polymeric molecular fuse enabling thermally responsive safety control without compromising electrochemical performance. By tuning inductive and hyperconjugative effects of phosphonate side chains, the dissociation energy of sacrificial P–C bonds is regulated, yielding an ∼10°C shift in activation temperature, as supported by density functional theory and in situ variable-temperature Raman spectroscopy. Upon activation, P-centered radicals suppress exothermic chain reactions, achieving a 76% reduction in heat release and delaying thermal runaway in LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes and 0.6 Ah Li-metal pouch cells. Notably, the activation threshold exceeds typical cathode processing temperatures, preventing premature radical generation during fabrication while enabling on-demand safety activation. This work establishes a substituent-regulated molecular fuse that couples fabrication-compatible stability with triggerable intrinsic safety, transforming battery thermal management from passive suppression to controllable molecular-level reaction pathways.

Helical Photonic Confinement of Narrowband-Emissive Carbon Quantum Dots Enables Amplified and Stimulus-Responsive Circularly Polarized Luminescence
authors: Wendi Qin, Jinyang Li, Jinsui Li, Chenhao Li, Kele Liao, Xun Zhang, and Fanglong Yuan
items.summary: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials that simultaneously exhibit large luminescence dissymmetry factors ( g lum ), high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), and dynamic optical addressability remain highly sought after yet challenging to realize. Here, we establish a CQDs-CLCs photonic coupling platform via helical photonic confinement of narrowband-emissive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in a chiral liquid crystal (CLC) host, enabling controlled emitter-photonic bandgap (PBG) spectral engineering. This yields amplified chiroptical signals with a g lum of up to 1.12 and a figure of merit (FM = g lum × PLQY) of 0.67. Beyond static performance, the helical photonic architecture allows dynamic CPL modulation by multiple stimuli, including temperature, light, electric field, mechanical pressure, viewing angle, and polarization. This work establishes helical photonic confinement as a material-photonic coupling strategy for decoupling dissymmetry amplification from emission efficiency while enabling multimodal stimulus-responsive modulation, offering potential applications in optical encryption, smart textiles, and photonic devices.

items.title: Incoherent diffraction imaging with a pseudo-thermal light source
authors: Pablo San Miguel Claveria, Peer Biesterfeld, Sebastião Antunes, Matilde Fernandes, Matilde Garcia, Matilde Nunes, Lucas Ansia Fernandez, Gareth O Williams, Sven Froehlich, David Theidel, Philip Mosel, Ihsan Fsaifes, Andrea Trabattoni, Marco Piccardo, Jean-Christophe Chanteloup, Milutin Kovacev, Hamed Merdji and Marta Fajardo
items.summary: Incoherent diffraction imaging—IDI—is a lensless imaging technique that has been recently proposed to exploit the partial coherence of incoherently scattered light to retrieve structural information from the scattering centers. Similar to the stellar intensity interferometry of Hanbury Brown and Twiss, the signal builds up on the second-order spatial correlations of the emitted light. The complex spatial distribution of the target is thereby encoded in the spatial intensity fluctuations of the scattered light. The first experimental realizations of this imaging technique have been realized using the fluorescence excited by an ultra-short x-ray pulse at free electron laser (FEL) facilities. Here, we propose an alternative setup based on a table-top pseudo-thermal light source that works as an optical emulator of the FEL experiment. This setup allows us to explore IDI under a wide range of physically relevant conditions as well as to benchmark numerical and analytical models currently used to determine the imaging capabilities of this technique.

items.title: Requirements for teleportation in an intercity quantum network
authors: Soubhadra Maiti, Guus Avis, Sounak Kar and Stephanie Wehner
items.summary: We investigate the hardware requirements for quantum teleportation in an intercity-scale network topology consisting of two metropolitan-scale networks connected via a long-distance backbone link. Specifically, we identify the minimal improvements required beyond the state-of-the-art to achieve an end-to-end expected teleportation fidelity of , which represents the classical limit. To this end, we formulate the hardware requirements computation as optimisation problems, where the hardware parameters representing the underlying device capabilities serve as decision variables. Assuming a simplified noise model, we derive closed-form analytical expressions for the teleportation fidelity and rate when the network is realised using heterogeneous quantum hardware, including a quantum repeater chain with a memory cut-off. Our derivations are based on events defined by the order statistics of link generation durations in both the metropolitan networks and the backbone, and the resulting expressions are verified against NetSquid simulations. The analytical expressions facilitate efficient exploration of the optimisation parameter space without resorting to computationally intensive simulations. We then apply this framework to a representative realisation in which the metropolitan nodes are based on trapped-ion processors and the backbone is composed of ensemble-based quantum memories. Our results suggest that teleportation across metropolitan distances already reaches the classical limit with state-of-the-art hardware when the data qubit is prepared after end-to-end entanglement has been established, whereas extending teleportation to intercity scales requires additional, though plausibly achievable, improvements in hardware performance.

items.title: Finite quantum pumps for phase-locked parametric amplification: requirements for quantum-battery work sources
items.summary: Quantum batteries have been proposed as locally precharged work sources for superconducting quantum technologies, suggesting a route to reduce continuously supplied microwave drives. Here we ask what a finite bosonic pump must provide to replace the pump tone of a nondegenerate parametric amplifier during a readout window. Quantizing the pump exposes a resource distinction hidden in the classical description: stored energy and the ordinary marginal signal response can survive pump phase twirling, whereas a reproducible phase-locked signal-idler field requires pump coherences in the number sectors coupled by the mixing process. In a closed trilinear model, a coherent pump and its number-matched phase-twirled counterpart generate the same number-like marginal observables, but only the coherent pump produces anomalous two-mode coherence and an EPR-squeezed interference dip. Including leakage, we collect the emitted fields into cascaded temporal modes. At matched collector bandwidth, the coherent pump gives the interference certifier , whereas the phase-randomized control gives . A weak seeded-signal analysis shows more sharply that an exact pump phase twirl leaves the collected signal marginal invariant by phase covariance while eliminating the anomalous signal-idler coherence. A finite-cutoff scan also indicates that weak amplitude squeezing can modestly deepen the phase-sensitive dip by reducing pump-number fluctuations while preserving most of the coherent displacement. Thus, for the three-wave-mixing pump families studied here, adjacent-number pump coherence is the resource that establishes a phase-locked joint amplifier field, rather than a prerequisite for energy transfer or ordinary marginal signal response.

items.title: Resolving carbon–timber trade-offs through age-structured forest management in China
items.summary: Abstract Forests are critical for climate mitigation, yet minimizing harvesting may accelerate forest aging and mortality, potentially constraining long-term carbon sequestration while increasing timber dependence. Using 15.5 million tree records from China’s National Forest Inventory and a spatially explicit forest dynamics model, we assessed how alternative harvesting strategies affect carbon storage and wood production through 2100 under climate change. We show that current low-intensity harvesting promotes forest aging and mortality over time, reducing carbon-retention efficiency. In contrast, age-structured and spatially differentiated harvesting, expanded to suitable multifunctional forests, maintains more dynamic forest age structures, lowers mortality losses, increases total forest carbon stocks by 4.2%, and enhances timber production by 38% relative to current management regime. Despite modest reductions in standing biomass, gains in harvested wood products and reduced mortality have potential to generate a net climate benefit. Our results demonstrate that optimizing forest age structure through rational harvesting can reconcile carbon sequestration and wood supply, providing a scalable pathway for sustainable forest management.

items.title: The 2025 Record Low in Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Dual Forcing from La Niña and Southern Indian Ocean Warm Anomaly
items.summary: Abstract In February-March 2025, the Arctic experienced record-low sea ice extent, despite a decadal slowdown in ice loss [1,2]. Although a weak La Niña was present, its influence alone is insufficient to explain this extreme event. Here, we demonstrate that this record low on an interannual scale was driven by the synergistic effects of La Niña and concurrent South Indian Ocean warm anomaly (SIOW). La Niña perturbed the Walker circulation, while SIOW altered the Hadley Cell. Their combined forcing over the tropical Indian Ocean generated intense anomalous downward motion and upper-level convergence, exciting a northeast-propagating Rossby wave. This wave train produced a significant anticyclonic anomaly over the Okhotsk Sea, which enhanced air temperature and accelerated sea ice melt. Our findings reveal an inter-basin atmospheric bridge, initiated by La Niña and SIOW, establishing the essential role of synergistic Indo-Pacific forcing in driving extreme Arctic sea ice loss, superimposed on a long‑term decline.

items.title: Bliss of dimensionality: How an unsupervised criterion identifies optimal low-resolution representations of high-dimensional datasets
items.summary: A systematic analysis of the resolution-relevance framework tests the possibility to identify informative low-resolution representations from empirical statistics alone in an unsupervised manner. Across synthetic, image-derived, and molecular datasets, increasing dimensionality or informative content progressively improves the method’s ability to select representations that preserve the underlying distribution, tracing the conditions under which data-driven resolution selection provides a faithful low-resolution description.

items.title: Emergent single-species non-reciprocity from bistable chemical dynamics
items.summary: Metson and Golestanian describe a new class of intelligent active matter systems in which non-reciprocal interactions emerge spontaneously in a homogeneous single-species, non-equilibrium chemically active suspension of microreactors. The work is based on a conceptual paradigm of emergent symmetries and their associated spontaneous symmetry breaking. The proposed framework gives a strong perspective of how lifelike traits of signaling, sensing, and propulsion can spontaneously and effortlessly emerge in such systems.

items.title: Synthetic data training for machine-learning-assisted ARPES experiments
authors: Meng Xing Na, Chris Zhou, Sydney K.Y. Dufresne, Matteo Michiardi, Andrea Damascelli
items.summary: Training artificial intelligence (AI) for experimental science usually requires huge collections of labeled data, which many techniques, such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), simply do not have. Na et al. show that synthetic ARPES data can fill the gap. They develop a high-fidelity ARPES simulator, aurelia, and train an AI model capable of judging the quality of real measurement data and of picking up the best spot to measure on the sample surface more precisely than a conventional analysis, highlighting the potential of AI-assisted experiments.

items.title: A comprehensive benchmark of an Ising machine on the Max-Cut problem
authors: Salwa Shaglel, Markus Kirsch, Marten Winkler, Christian Münch, Stefan Walter, Fritz Schinkel and Martin Kliesch
items.summary: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulations of combinatorial optimization problems allow for solving them using various quantum heuristics. While large-scale quantum computations are currently still out of reach, we can already numerically test such QUBO formulations on a perhaps surprisingly large scale. In this work, we benchmark Fujitsu’s Digital Annealer (DA) on the Max-Cut problem, which captures the main complexity of the QUBO problem. We make a comprehensive benchmark against leading other heuristic algorithms on graphs with up to 53,000 variables by focusing on the wall-clock time. Moreover, we compare the DA performance against published performance results of the D-Wave hybrid quantum–classical annealer and the recently proposed QIS3 heuristic. Based on performance statistics for over 2000 graphs from the MQLib, we find that the DA yields competitive results. We hope that this benchmark demonstrates the extent to which large QUBO instances can be heuristically solved today, yielding consistent results across different solvers.

items.title: A field-quadrature perspective on strong-field ionization with squeezed light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Jianmin Yuan and Xu Wang
items.summary: Bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) has emerged as a macroscopic nonclassical light source capable of driving strong-field processes. Yet its broad, long-tailed photon-number distribution bears little resemblance to the narrow poissonian distribution of a coherent field, obscuring how the corresponding strong-field responses are connected. We show that field-quadrature space supplies the missing continuous description: coherent, squeezed coherent, and BSV states are Gaussian wave packets distinguished only by their centers and widths. This representation provides a unified framework for tracing the coherent-to-BSV transition at fixed mean photon number and for analyzing both ionization yields and photoelectron spectra. Crucially, BSV is a symmetry-protected endpoint in quadrature space. Near the BSV limit, we identify a simple scaling law of the ionization response associated with a residual coherent component. We show that this scaling arises from parity-induced stationarity with respect to the Gaussian center, together with the accompanying width variation near the BSV limit. The result provides a symmetry-based criterion for approaching the BSV regime and a potential probe of a mode-matched coherent displacement through the strong-field response itself.

items.title: Self-testing of logical subspaces of quantum error-correcting codes
items.summary: We develop explicit device-independent self-testing constructions for logical subspaces of quantum error-correcting codes. By constructing multipartite Bell inequalities tailored to stabilizer code structures, we show that maximal quantum violations uniquely certify that the underlying shared state resides within the logical subspace of a given code, up to local isometries. These constructions extend earlier stabilizer-subspace self-testing results beyond the five-qubit code to several representative stabilizer codes, including the six-qubit code, the Steane code, and Shor’s nine-qubit code. The tilted sum-of-squares variants further impose algebraic constraints on the relative weights of the logical sectors. Together, these results provide explicit examples of device-independent self-testing for representative stabilizer-code logical subspaces and suggest possible directions for verification and benchmarking of encoded quantum information.

items.title: Anatomy of spin-orbit torques in monolayer ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$ and ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$: Insights from atomistic and momentum-space decompositions

Horizontal mirror symmetry forbids conventional in-plane spin accumulation for out-of-plane magnetization, while tilting the magnetization enables a strongly angle-dependent response. Combining density functional theory, Wannier interpolation, and Kubo formalism, they map the torque across the magnetization sphere. They reveal hidden torques on mirror-related Fe atoms up to 30 times the net torque, whose cancellation could be lifted through van der Waals engineering.
