items.title: A quantum optical concept of attosecond pulses: the attoquants
items.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) is conventionally understood to produce attosecond pulse trains only when the emitted harmonics are mutually phase-locked, in accordance with the classical theory of mode-locking. In a quantum optical framework, pulse synthesis would also require a regular phase relation between the components, when the harmonic field is in a separable multimode quantum state. This requirement, however, can be circumvented for harmonic combs exhibiting intermodal entanglement. We introduce a novel family of multimode quantum states, termed attoquants: states associated with highly structured pulse trains that are inherently insensitive to relative phases. As a concrete example, we analyse the coherent permanent state, constructed as a completely symmetric superposition of products of coherent states over all permutations of a fixed parameter set. It is shown analytically that its electric-field mean value is a locked Fourier superposition of the driving-field harmonics, yielding an attosecond pulse train without requiring regular phase relations between the high-harmonic components. We further calculate the photon statistics, the Wigner function, and the logarithmic negativity of these states, in order to show their genuinely nonclassical character, and the degree of entanglement. Finally, we offer a phenomenological interpretation for the generation of such entangled states during HHG, as a consequence of multi-atom effects. Since the coherence volume of the driving field greatly exceeds that of its harmonics, a collectively-driven cluster of atoms can radiate the harmonics as spatially separated, but classically indistinguishable sources. This can generate the permutation-symmetric entanglement structure of an attoquant.

items.title: Exact Finite Response of Higher-Order Statistics in Nonequilibrium Networks
authors: Ruicheng Bao, Shiling Liang and 师翎 梁
items.summary: We develop an exact finite-perturbation response theory for the higher-order statistics of general state observables in nonequilibrium Markov networks. For local perturbations, the moment generating function obeys an exact nonlinear response identity in the perturbation strength, controlled by a single kinetic parameter α. This induces an exact nonlinear map for the cumulant generating function and closed expressions for finite responses of all cumulants through partial Bell polynomials. As a central application, we obtain a complete theory of variance control, including sharp saturation limits, a classification of monotone-suppression and sign-reversal regimes, and mean-first-passage-time design principles for optimal noise suppression. The same framework yields exact formulas for operational and symmetrized response resolution along the accessible control branch. A four-state gene-regulation model illustrates how local kinetic control suppresses the occupancy noise of a transcriptionally competent promoter state.

items.title: A Collision-State Criterion for Two-Peak Collisions in a Two-Dimensional Long-Wave–Short-Wave Resonance Interaction System
authors: Wei Dong, 伟 董, Houhui Yi, 厚会 伊, Xiaofeng Li, 晓凤 李, Muwei Liu, 慕威 刘, Zhiyang Zhang and 之阳 张
items.summary: This Letter investigates the finite-time morphology of two-pulse collisions in a two-dimensional long-wave–short-wave resonance interaction system with a local cubic perturbation. An integral identity for the centered second moment separates the collision dynamics into contributions from dispersive spreading, local quartic overlap, and long-wave feedback. For the prescribed two-sech initial-data family and the finite observation interval T ≤ 7, these contributions distinguish double-peak and single-peak morphologies with an accuracy of 94.17%. A feedforward neural network is then employed to efficiently reconstruct the distribution of the identity-based result in the parameter plane of the nonintegrable coefficient and relative phase. This distribution shows that variation of the relative phase can change the collision morphology.

items.title: NextCrystal: A Symmetry-Driven Generative Framework for Crystal Structure Prediction
authors: Jinming Mu, 锦铭 穆, Lixin He, 力新 何, Xudong Zhu, 旭东 朱, Shi Yin and 实 殷
items.summary: Crystal structure prediction (CSP), which aims to predict the 3D atomic arrangement of a crystal from its composition, is central to materials discovery and mechanistic understanding. Crystal symmetry plays a crucial role in CSP, but given the composition in a unit cell, existing methods either struggle with the NP-hard combinatorial challenge of enforcing symmetry rigorously or rely on retrieving known templates, inherently limiting both physical fidelity and the discovery of genuinely new materials. To address this challenge, we introduce NextCrystal, a symmetry-driven generative framework that employs language models to encode chemical semantics and directly generate fine-grained Wyckoff site patterns from atomic stoichiometry, without retrieving pre-existing structural templates at inference. To overcome the combinatorial complexity of site assignments, we incorporate domain knowledge via an efficient, linear-complexity heuristic beam search, rigorously enforcing algebraic consistency between site multiplicities and atomic stoichiometry. By integrating this symmetry-consistent template into a diffusion backbone, the framework constrains the stochastic generative trajectory to a physically plausible geometric manifold. NextCrystal achieves state-of-the-art performance on stability, uniqueness, and novelty benchmarks, as well as superior structural matching, establishing a paradigm for exploring previously unexplored crystallographic space without relying on prior structural templates. As a blind-rediscovery case study, NextCrystal recovers the known low-energy antipolar oV Pnma polymorph of HfO2, which is absent from the training dataset, without retrieving a structural prototype during inference. Standardized structure matching after a common first-principles relaxation confirms its equivalence to the published oV/a62 structure and its distinction from the conventional high-pressure cotunnite/oII Pnma phase.

items.title: Thermal Signatures of the Slater–Mott Crossover in the Hubbard Model: From Double Occupancy to Antiferromagnetic Correlation Length
authors: Mingzhong Lu, 明忠 卢, Yu-Feng Song, 育峰 宋, Youjin Deng, 友金 邓, Yuan-Yao He and 院耀 何
items.summary: The interaction-driven crossover from a Slater insulator to a Mott insulator in the Néel-ordered ground state of the Hubbard model is a fundamental paradigm of strongly correlated electrons, yet its quantitative characterization has remained elusive. Here we establish a clear and experimentally accessible thermal criterion for this crossover via the sign change of the temperature derivative of double occupancy, (∂D/∂T)U, near zero temperature. In the Slater regime, (∂D/∂T)U > 0 reflects the major role of charge fluctuations; in the Mott regime, the anomalous (∂D/∂T)U < 0, a manifestation of the Pomeranchuk effect, signals the dominance of low-energy spin superexchange physics. Using exact diagonalization and numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this criterion determines the crossover boundary at Ucross/t = 4.0(2) for the half-filled two-dimensional Hubbard model. Furthermore, we obtain a consistent boundary independently from the maximum in the antiferromagnetic correlation length, which also arises from the superexchange physics. These two thermal signatures are theoretically unified through the local minimum of thermal entropy versus interaction U at low temperatures. Our results offer a direct, measurable, and physically intuitive framework to identify the SlaterMott crossover in optical lattice experiments.

items.title: Ultrathin BiO x Charge-Transfer Doping for Cross-TMD Electronic Modulation and Homogeneous WSe 2 Inverters
authors: Ching-Hao Hsu, Yu-Wei Hsu, Ta-Wei Hsu, Yu-Tung Lin, Li-Ya Chiu, I-Chih Ni, and Chih-I Wu
items.summary: Abstract Charge-transfer doping provides a nondestructive route to tune two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), but selectively patterned n-type dopants effective across different TMD channels remain limited. Here, ultrathin bismuth oxide (BiO x ) is used as an n-type charge-transfer doping and passivation layer for monolayer MoS 2 and WSe 2 transistors. Thicker BiO x strengthens n-type modulation but reduces gate controllability. The modulation remains stable after ambient storage and air annealing. BiO x also enhances electron transport in WSe 2 and enables homogeneous WSe 2 inverters with MoO x -doped p-FETs, achieving a gain of ∼19 and a total normalized noise margin of 0.895 V DD at V DD = 2 V. items.title: Engineering High-Entropy Tetrahedrite Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S Nanocrystals via Sequential Cation Exchange as Efficient Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reactions
authors: Ankita Bora, Suvodeep Sen, Niraj Nitish Patil, Temilade Esther Edgoke, Kevin M. Ryan, and Shalini Singh
items.summary: Abstract High-entropy chalcogenides represent an emerging class of functional materials with immense potential in broad applications. To date, colloidal high-entropy nanocrystals (NCs) have predominantly been accessed via co-nucleation of precursors or simultaneous incorporation of multiple cations. While effective, these approaches lack a mechanistic understanding of NC synthesis. Here, we report the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy Cu–Zn–Sb–Ag–Bi–S NCs in the tetrahedrite phase, employing a sequential, low-temperature cation-exchange strategy, starting from a Cu–Zn–Sb–S tetrahedrite template. Subsequent sequential cation exchanges preserve the crystal phase while enabling precise control over morphology. This bottom-up approach circumvents the need for high-temperature synthesis, while allowing isolation and characterization of intermediate states, providing important mechanistic insight into the evolution of high-entropy NCs. The nanocrystals served as hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts with less negative cathodic potentials. This work introduces the high-entropy tetrahedrite phase, paving the way for entropy-stabilized chalcogenides for energy conversion applications.

items.title: Precursor-Free Photoelectrochemical Fabrication of Spiral Lead Oxide Nanostructures under Circularly Polarized Light
authors: Ami Hayakawa, Tetsu Tatsuma, and Hiroyasu Nishi
items.summary: Abstract Chiral nanostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their strong interactions with circularly polarized light (CPL) and their various applications. Although various fabrication methods have been reported, photoelectrochemical approaches using CPL as the chiral source are attractive because of their simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and scalability. However, previous CPL-based methods have required two or more steps, including the preparation of anisotropic precursors. Here, we demonstrate a single-step method for the selective growth of chiral PbO 2 nanostructures with handedness dictated by CPL at a chiral yield of 87%, by simply irradiating a transparent electrode with CPL, without using precursor nanoparticles. The obtained structures exhibit well-defined spiral morphologies and high chiroptical activity with maximum dissymmetry factors (g-factors) ranging from 0.006 to 0.010. This conceptual framework, involving symmetry breaking through random nucleation and Mie-resonance-mediated spiral growth under CPL, may be applicable to the template-free fabrication of various chiral nanomaterials.

items.title: Pressure Engineering through Silica Nanoconfinement for Melting Point Elevation of Gold Nanoparticles
authors: Chang-Won Choi, Jeong Hun Choi, Gi-Yeop Kim, In Su Lee, and Si-Young Choi
items.summary: Abstract Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO 2 ) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point ( T m ) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO 2 -encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO 2 ) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO 2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4–5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO 2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater T m elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.

items.title: Magnetism beyond the Monolayer: Long-Range Order in an Interfacial Phase of CoBr 2
authors: Samuel Kerschbaumer, David Serrate, Adriana Elizabet Candia, Andrea Aguirre, Danilo Longo, Fadi Choueikani, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Pavel Jelínek, Maxim Ilyn, Celia Rogero, and Sebastien E. Hadjadj
items.summary: Abstract Transition metal dihalides are promising magnetic van der Waals materials because of their structural simplicity, chemical stability, and compatibility with nanofabrication. While magnetic order in these systems is typically associated with bulk-like monolayers, its relation to interfacial phases remains largely unexplored. Here we show that in CoBr 2 grown on Au(111), long-range magnetic order already emerges in a structurally distinct interfacial precursor phase, prior to the formation of the bulk-like monolayer. During growth, this phase evolves into the monolayer, accompanied by a transition from molecular-like states to semiconducting behavior. Spin-resolved STM reveals an inhomogeneous in-plane magnetic response that is locally suppressed by point defects, whereas macroscopic XMCD demonstrates robust long-range order with pronounced in-plane anisotropy. These results establish that long-range magnetic order in CoBr 2 does not require an ideal bulk-like monolayer but can emerge from interfacial phases with distinct electronic and structural properties, enabling magnetism beyond the monolayer limit.

items.title: Wrinkled Pd Metallene: Synergistic Geometric and Electronic Engineering for High-Performance Bioorthogonal Catalysis
authors: Yiming Ma, Yanjie Zhang, Yanjun Ji, Huan Wang, Anjun Song, Ying Wang, Fang Pu, Jinsong Ren, and Xiaogang Qu
items.summary: Abstract Palladium-mediated bioorthogonal catalysis enables in situ activation of therapeutic and diagnostic agents within living systems, yet developing high-efficacy catalysts remains challenging. Herein, we report a wrinkled Pd metallene catalyst (Pd ML) in which nanoscale wrinkling generates abundant active sites and induces lattice strain, thereby optimizing the electronic and geometric configurations of the catalytic centers for high-performance bioorthogonal catalysis. The Pd MLs exhibit substantially enhanced catalytic activity compared to Pd nanoparticles and their wrinkle-free counterpart, flat Pd metallene. Theoretical calculations reveal that the wrinkle-induced lattice strain shifts the d-band center of Pd downward, thereby facilitating the bioorthogonal reaction. Following functionalization with the AS1411 aptamer, the Pd MLs enable targeted activation of an antitumor prodrug and realize efficient tumor suppression both in vitro and in vivo. This work represents the first example of enhancing bioorthogonal catalysis via synergistic geometric and electronic engineering, establishing a rational paradigm for the development of high-performance bioorthogonal catalysts.

items.title: Third-Harmonic Generation in Crumpled Silicon Nanomembranes
authors: Gwanjin Lee, Ajit K. Katiyar, Jong-Hyun Ahn, Hyunmin Kim, and JaeDong Lee
items.summary: Abstract Silicon nanomembranes provide mechanically compliant devices for strain engineering. Here, we investigate third-harmonic generation in flat and crumpled silicon nanomembranes of 15 and 35 nm using polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation microscopy with ab initio calculations. In flat silicon nanomembranes, the measured polarization dependence is reproduced by the calculated third-order susceptibility, identifying the intrinsic nonlinear response of silicon. In crumpled silicon nanomembranes, local strain variations between valleys and apexes generate distinct polarization-dependent responses. Uniaxial strain along the [110] direction breaks electronic structure symmetry and induces anisotropy between X- and Y-polarized components, while the real and imaginary parts of the third-order susceptibility exhibit quadratic strain dependence. Morphology-induced redistribution of the local optical field further modifies the response in crumpled geometry, and a finite-difference time-domain-based local-field correction substantially improves agreement with the experiment. Therefore, the third-harmonic response of crumpled silicon nanomembranes is controlled by both strain-induced electronic structure modification and morphology-induced local optical-field redistribution.

items.title: Polarization-Dependent Topological Phase Reconstruction via Multipolarization-Controlled Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya Interaction
authors: Haoming Su, Xiong-Xiong Xue, Yee Sin Ang, Ke-Qiu Chen, and Li-Ming Tang
items.summary: Abstract Conventional antiferroelectric states generally suppress the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) and enable skyrmion erasure by restoring inversion symmetry. However, noncentrosymmetric antiferroelectric states preserve broken inversion symmetry, offering an additional dimension for manipulating DMI and topological magnetic phases. Here, combining first-principles calculations with atomistic simulations, we demonstrate polarization-driven reconstruction of the DMI vector field and topological magnetic phases in monolayer CuCrP 2 Se 6 . FE u -AFE-FE d polarization switching enables the evolution of a uniform DMI into an anisotropic DMI vector field by reconstructing the lattice symmetry, thereby achieving reversible control between topologically nontrivial skyrmions and topologically trivial magnetic bubbles. These findings establish DMI vector-field reconstruction in noncentrosymmetric AFE states as a mechanism for engineering magnetic topology beyond conventional DMI reversal (D → −D) or suppression (D → 0).

items.summary: we report on signatures of classical chaos in ultracold collisions between a trapped ion and a free atom. Using numerical simulations, we show that the scattering dynamics can be highly sensitive to initial conditions for various mass ratios and trapping frequencies, indicating the onset of chaos. We quantify this chaotic dynamics by calculating its fractal dimension. We show that for a trapped Sr ion and a free Rb atom chaotic dynamic appears under experimentally relevant conditions, and find its characteristic energy scale. The observation of classical chaos in atom-trapped-ion collisions suggests that signatures of quantum chaos might appear, for example, through a Wigner–Dyson distribution of collisional resonances.
